correctness.rationale: Reconstructed ordered equivalence classes and exact weight n!/product(s_i!). The quantifier-rank q truncation of block size to min(q,s) respects the q-round EF game; coloured word q-types form finite aperiodic concatenation monoid. The exact EGF is e(I-K(z))^-1 v with K=sum B_a(z)T_a. At rho=log 2, P=K(rho) is stochastic, recurrent classes have self-loops from aperiodicity so P^n tends to harmonic projection H, and HK'(rho)H=2H; semisimple peripheral eigenvalue produces H/[2(rho-z)]. All nonreal |z|=rho have strict row-norm deficit from consecutive positive degrees in B_q(z); the simple pole is isolated and coefficient ratio to (2-e^z)^-1 converges exponentially. Matrix entries lie in Q(rho); finite absorption systems yield L. Independent weighted composition enumeration and endpoint first/last-block count checked n<=7, not infinite argument.

originality.rationale: Strong directly relevant precursor Braunfeld and Kukla (2022) establishes an UNLABELLED composition limit law and explicitly asks in Section 5, Question 5.1 whether COMPOSITIONS admit a LABELED logical limit law. Labeled compositions are precisely total preorders with the n!/product(s_i!) probabilities used here. The older theorem does not entail this sampled-model answer; the current result gives exponential convergence and an exact field, directly addressing the published question. Other finite-word monoid and ordered Bell tools are classical; generic weighted-word limit theorems remain a subsumption priority risk.

value.rationale: A complete effective FO limit law for a canonical random labelled combinatorial structure, with geometric rates and nontrivial log2 boundary probability, directly answers a documented open problem about labelled compositions. This is substantial model-theoretic value without claiming zero-one behaviour or uniform sentence complexity.

final_claim: Every first-order {R}-sentence under the uniform labelled n-element total-preorder measure has probability L+O(c^n), with 0<c<1 depending on sentence and effectively computable L in Q(log2); no zero-one law.
limitations: Uniform labelled total preorders in one binary relation only; sentence-dependent rate; no result for unlabelled random ordered compositions, arbitrary preorders or expanded vocabularies.
